blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Batching Variable-Length Trajectories**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Batching Variable-Length Trajectories
blocks.md: Consider a batch where a 30-turn debugging and code-repair trace shares a training buffer with a brief, one-turn file lookup. Under an ordinary lower-triangular causal mask, the lookup can attend directly to the repair trace's intermediate file contents and tool outputs, context that the lookup policy will never have at serving time. Under token averaging, the multi-turn repair trace also outweighs the brief lookup by the ratio of their active target tokens.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Loss normalization across variable-length examples
- Example isolation in packed buffers
- Position conventions and equivalence checks

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Loss normalization matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.

questions.q: The section **Batching Variable-Length Trajectories** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A disagreement rate measured on reference prefixes bounds excess task cost only by min(H, H^2 eps), while the same rate on learner states with bounded recovery cost gives a linear bound, so where imitation error is measured sets the horizon penalty.
Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.
LoRA cuts trainable parameters but parameter state falls only by the byte ratio of trainable to frozen state, and adapters give modularity, not isolation.

Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.

questions.explanation: This section develops **Loss normalization**: Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.
